intro: Transportation engineers plan roads, transit and traffic systems, skills used in planning, logistics and environmental work. The closest of the 25 careers below is Civil Engineering Technologists and Technicians, with an 88% skill match, and Transportation Planners are 87% matched with a BLS May 2025 median of $101,110 for their broader group.
why_it_works: Your work is modeling how people and vehicles move, then designing changes that are safe, affordable and approved. O*NET rates complex problem solving, judgment and time management at 3.88 out of 5 for this job. Planning, logistics and water resources work use the same analysis. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Transportation planning keeps your expertise but shifts toward policy and public engagement.
Logistics Engineers are an 82% match if you want to move from roads to supply chains.
Learn programming for traffic simulation; it is one of your most common skill gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former transportation engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are civil engineering technologists (88%), Transportation Planners (87%) and Logistics Engineers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Traffic Technicians are also 80% matched, with a median of $59,090, and work on signal timing and traffic studies.

faq.q: Which jobs for transportation engineers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Water Resource Specialists at $167,220, brownfield redevelopment specialists at $141,900 and wind energy development managers at $141,900, according to BLS May 2025 data. These figures are for broader BLS groups, so check pay for the specific role where you live.

faq.q: Do transportation engineers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than transportation engineers already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 55% of workers in a close match, while 3 matches need a graduate degree.

faq.q: What skills should transportation engineers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, equipment selection, negotiation and programming. Systems analysis already rates 3.75 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so technical tools and stakeholder negotiation are the main steps for most moves.
